SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A plant with no water for many days will (1 mark)
   A. Become weak and may die
   B. Make more flowers
   C. Get stronger
   D. Grow faster

2. How many legs does an insect have? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Ten
   C. Six
   D. Four

3. What is the waste passed out by animals called? (1 mark)
   A. Urine and faeces
   B. Food
   C. Milk
   D. Seeds

4. Which of these is a crab? (1 mark)
   A. An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   B. A bird
   C. A mammal
   D. A vertebrate with fur

5. What does deworming do? (1 mark)
   A. Kills worms in the intestines
   B. Cleans teeth
   C. Makes food taste better
   D. Cures a cough

6. Which part of the digestive system is the widest tube near the end? (1 mark)
   A. Gullet
   B. Anus
   C. Large intestine
   D. Small intestine

7. Why should you chew your food well? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food heavier
   B. It makes food colder
   C. It stops you drinking water
   D. It makes food smaller for easier digestion

8. Where does the digestive tube end? (1 mark)
   A. Gullet
   B. Mouth
   C. Anus
   D. Stomach

9. Which of these helps prevent germs entering the food? (1 mark)
   A. Covering food
   B. Putting food on the floor
   C. Leaving food open
   D. Letting flies land on food

10. Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Solid
   C. Liquid
   D. Powder

11. Which state of matter is used in a cooking gas cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Powder
   C. Solid
   D. Ice

12. Which of these is a solid? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. A stone
   C. Air
   D. Steam

13. Which of these can be poured and takes the shape of its container? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Stone
   C. Book
   D. Brick

14. Which waste goes into a compost pit? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bags
   B. Tins
   C. Vegetable peelings
   D. Glass

15. What does reduce mean? (1 mark)
   A. Use again
   B. Make less waste
   C. Make into new items
   D. Burn waste

16. Why should waste bins have lids? (1 mark)
   A. To make waste heavier
   B. To make them look nice
   C. To make waste rot faster
   D. To keep out flies and rats

17. Which is the best order of managing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Recycle, reuse, reduce
   B. Reduce, reuse, recycle
   C. Burn, bury, throw
   D. Throw, burn, bury

18. Which of these is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Steam
   B. Smoke
   C. Dirty bath water
   D. A banana peel

19. Which of these describes recycling water? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting water
   B. Letting water evaporate
   C. Boiling it and throwing it
   D. Cleaning used water so it can be used again

20. Who should practise water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Only farmers
   C. Only adults
   D. Everyone at home and school

21. Why should we not throw waste in rivers? (1 mark)
   A. It helps fish
   B. It makes water clean
   C. It makes water sweet
   D. It pollutes the water

22. What does drip irrigation do? (1 mark)
   A. Floods the whole field
   B. Cleans the soil
   C. Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   D. Makes rain

23. Which of these is NOT a way to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Harvesting rainwater
   B. Washing dishes under a running tap
   C. Using a basin
   D. Fixing leaks

24. What is mulching? (1 mark)
   A. Burning grass
   B. Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   C. Removing all plants
   D. Digging deep holes

25. Which of these is a way of reducing friction on a bicycle chain? (1 mark)
   A. Wetting it with mud
   B. Leaving it dry and rusty
   C. Adding sand
   D. Oiling it

26. Why does a mango fall from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Light pulls it
   B. Gravity pulls it down
   C. Friction pushes it
   D. Sound moves it

27. Which of these uses of light is for plants? (1 mark)
   A. Making roots taller
   B. Making them bend downward
   C. Making them cold
   D. Making their own food

28. What is a transparent material? (1 mark)
   A. A material that is always red
   B. A material that blocks all light
   C. A material that lets almost all light pass through
   D. A material that makes light

29. You want to see if a material is opaque. What do you do? (1 mark)
   A. Smell it
   B. Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   C. Weigh it
   D. Taste it

30. Why is it better to use daylight than electric light in the day? (1 mark)
   A. It makes rooms dark
   B. It costs more
   C. It saves money
   D. It is unsafe

31. Which of these is NOT a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. A candle
   C. A mirror
   D. An electric bulb

32. Which of these makes its own light? (1 mark)
   A. A shiny cup
   B. A white wall
   C. A glow-worm
   D. A mirror

33. What is one benefit of using translucent roof sheets in a house? (1 mark)
   A. It uses more electricity
   B. It blocks the sun completely
   C. It makes the house dark
   D. It saves electricity in the day

34. Which battery-powered device gives artificial light? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Firefly
   C. Stars
   D. Torch

35. Why are pot handles often made of wood or plastic? (1 mark)
   A. They get very hot
   B. They are heavy
   C. They pass heat slowly
   D. They pass heat quickly

36. Which use of heat helps farmers to store maize? (1 mark)
   A. Colouring paper
   B. Drying grain
   C. Making shadows
   D. Writing

37. Which of these is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Firewood
   C. Sand
   D. Clean water

38. Why should pupils not touch hot sufurias? (1 mark)
   A. They become cold
   B. They become bigger
   C. They can burn their skin
   D. They make sound

39. Which of these uses heat to change dough into bread? (1 mark)
   A. Baking
   B. Freezing
   C. Washing
   D. Cutting

40. What is heat? (1 mark)
   A. A form of energy that makes things hot
   B. A kind of matter
   C. A type of gas
   D. A kind of sound

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials. (3 marks)

42. Name four safety measures to observe in a kitchen and give a reason for each. (4 marks)

43. State two uses of light. (2 marks)

44. Plan a project to sensitise your community about the importance of water conservation. State the steps. (5 marks)

45. Explain why we should care for animals and describe how it can be done at home and at school. (5 marks)

46. A ball is at rest. Kelvin kicks it, then Mercy stops it with her foot, then she kicks it to the right. Name the effect of the force in each case. (3 marks)

47. Explain why steam from a kettle is invisible although we see a white cloud above the spout. Say what state of matter the cloud is. (5 marks)

48. Give four healthy eating habits that keep the digestive system healthy. (4 marks)

49. Write three ways of managing waste in the classroom. (3 marks)

50. A pupil grows two bean seedlings. One is put in a cupboard and the other in the sunlight. Both are watered. After a week the two look different. Describe what she might see and give a reason. (4 marks)

51. Describe how you would show that air takes up space using a cup, tissue paper and a basin of water. (4 marks)

52. Why should you not touch a hot object to find out how hot it is? What should you use? (3 marks)

53. Describe how to make a pair of kitchen gloves from local materials. (4 marks)

54. Why should we use LED and solar lamps instead of paraffin lamps? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

55. Describe how animals respond to changes around them. Give four examples. (4 marks)

56. Describe how waste attracts pests that harm health. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Become weak and may die
   Water is needed for life, so a plant without it wilts and may die.

2. C — Six
   All adult insects have six legs.

3. A — Urine and faeces
   Animals remove waste such as urine and faeces.

4. A — An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
   A crab has no backbone and has a hard shell outside.

5. A — Kills worms in the intestines
   Deworming tablets kill worms living in the intestines.

6. C — Large intestine
   The large intestine is wider than the small intestine.

7. D — It makes food smaller for easier digestion
   Chewing breaks food into small pieces.

8. C — Anus
   Waste leaves the body through the anus.

9. A — Covering food
   Covering food keeps out flies and dirt.

10. A — Gas
   Gases spread out to fill all the space.

11. A — Gas
   Cooking gas is a gas that burns to give heat.

12. B — A stone
   A stone keeps its shape.

13. A — Water
   Water is a liquid.

14. C — Vegetable peelings
   Only decomposable waste is composted.

15. B — Make less waste
   To reduce is to make less waste.

16. D — To keep out flies and rats
   Covered bins reduce smell and pests.

17. B — Reduce, reuse, recycle
   First make less waste, then reuse, then recycle.

18. D — A banana peel
   A banana peel is a solid thrown away.

19. D — Cleaning used water so it can be used again
   Recycling cleans water for another use.

20. D — Everyone at home and school
   Everyone shares water and should save it.

21. D — It pollutes the water
   Waste makes water dirty and unsafe.

22. C — Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   It gives water slowly at the roots.

23. B — Washing dishes under a running tap
   A running tap wastes water.

24. B — Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   Mulch reduces evaporation from the soil.

25. D — Oiling it
   Oil helps parts slide.

26. B — Gravity pulls it down
   Gravity acts on every object.

27. D — Making their own food
   Plants use light to make food.

28. C — A material that lets almost all light pass through
   Transparent materials let us see clearly through them.

29. B — Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   If no light passes, it is opaque.

30. C — It saves money
   Sunlight is free.

31. C — A mirror
   A mirror only reflects light.

32. C — A glow-worm
   Glow-worms produce their own light.

33. D — It saves electricity in the day
   Daylight comes in so lamps are not needed.

34. D — Torch
   A torch is made by people.

35. C — They pass heat slowly
   Handles stay cooler.

36. B — Drying grain
   Heat dries wet things.

37. B — Firewood
   Fuels burn to give heat.

38. C — They can burn their skin
   Hot metal burns.

39. A — Baking
   Baking uses heat.

40. A — A form of energy that makes things hot
   Heat is a form of energy.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials do not let light through.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Handles inwards to avoid knocking pots, gloves to avoid burns, children away to avoid accidents, switch off iron to avoid fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with reason.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: To see, for safety, to discourage pests, for plants to make food, to dry clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a message, make posters, put them near taps and gates, speak at assembly, do a demonstration of saving water and check results.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals give us milk, meat, eggs and honey and help us in work. They are part of nature. We give them food, water, shelter and medical care and we do not hurt them. At school we keep the compound safe for birds.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for ways.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kelvin starts motion, Mercy stops motion, Mercy's second kick changes direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct effect.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Steam is water as a gas and it is invisible. The white cloud is made of tiny water drops which are liquid.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for steam is a gas, 1 mark for invisible, 1 mark for white cloud being tiny drops, 1 mark for liquid, 1 mark for a clear explanation.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Eat a balanced diet, eat fruits and vegetables, drink clean water, chew slowly, wash fruits, avoid rotten food, cover food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each habit up to 4.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a bin with a lid, put paper in a separate box for reusing, do not litter, make monitors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant in the cupboard looks weak and pale and the one in the light is green and healthy. Plants need light to make food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for describing each plant and 2 marks for the reason.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Push dry tissue into the bottom of the cup. Turn the cup upside down and push it straight down into water. Lift it out. The tissue is dry because air took up the space in the cup and kept the water out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for pushing into water, 1 mark for dry tissue, 1 mark for conclusion.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can burn your skin. Use a thermometer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for burns, 1 mark for using a thermometer, 1 mark for reason it is safe.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose thick cotton cloth or old towel. Trace and cut two mitten shapes. Add an inner layer. Sew them together leaving the wrist open. Turn it inside out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are safer with less fire risk and less smoke. Solar lamps use free energy and are cheaper to use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: A goat lifts its head at noise, a snail pulls into its shell when touched, birds fly away from danger, animals seek shade in hot weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each of three examples.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rotting waste attracts flies, rats and cockroaches. They spread germs to food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea and cholera.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pests, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for diseases.
